# Autoimmune liver disease overlap syndromes

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Diseases of the liver > Autoimmune liver disease overlap syndromes*

[Original Article Link](/library/H90KKR)

---

## Summary

Autoimmune <u>liver</u> disease overlap syndromes are conditions that manifest with features of more than one autoimmune <u>liver</u> disease, most commonly <u>autoimmune hepatitis</u> (<u>AIH</u>) with <u>primary biliary cholangitis</u> (<u>PBC</u>) or <u>primary sclerosing cholangitis</u> (<u>PSC</u>). These syndromes are considered clinical descriptions rather than distinct pathological entities. The <u>AIH-PBC overlap syndrome</u> is more common in women, while the <u>AIH-PSC overlap syndrome</u> is more common in younger men and is strongly associated with <u>inflammatory bowel disease</u> (<u>IBD</u>). Diagnosis of <u>AIH-PBC overlap</u> requires features of both conditions, including <u>elevated transaminases</u> and <u>cholestatic</u> <u>liver</u> injury, specific <u>autoantibodies</u>, and <u>histology</u> findings of <u>interface hepatitis</u> and florid <u>bile</u> duct lesions. Diagnosis of <u>AIH-PSC overlap</u> requires probable or definite <u>AIH</u>, negative <u>antimitochondrial antibodies</u> (<u>AMA</u>), and <u>cholangiographic</u> evidence of <u>PSC</u>. <u>AIH-cholestatic syndrome</u> is an autoimmune <u>liver</u> disease characterized by <u>AIH</u> with <u>cholestatic</u> <u>liver</u> injury that does not meet the diagnostic criteria for <u>PBC</u> or <u>PSC</u>. Treatment is directed at the predominant disease, typically involving combination therapy with <u>ursodeoxycholic acid</u> and <u>immunosuppressants</u> (e.g., <u>glucocorticoids</u>). Overlap syndromes are associated with an increased risk of <u>cirrhosis</u>, treatment failure, and a need for <u>liver transplant</u>.
